sample_delivery_exceptions::recommendati.text: {"recommendation":{"statement":"Prioritise ALT-04: trace and repair the loss of secondary address lines (unit/apartment/suite) between checkout and the delivery label, scoped explicitly to the apartment segment, and pair it with the minimum slice of ALT-03's instrumentation needed to measure it. This is the only candidate that attacks the largest exception category in the worst-performing segment with converging qualitative and ticket evidence, no new vendor, no driver-app dependency, and no per-delivery cost increase. It is a recommendation, not a decision: the effort has not been localised or estimated, so approve a time-boxed localisation spike first and hold the build commitment until the spike reports. If the spike shows the field is lost in a system that cannot be changed before Q3 2026, fall back to ALT-03 rather than to ALT-07.","option_kind":"data_quality","selected_alternative_id":"ALT-04","claims":[{"id":"C1","statement":"Within the apartment segment, address_error is the largest exception category (37.3% of apartment tickets, 921 tickets in 2026-Q2), and the ticket notes attribute it specifically to missing or wrong unit numbers.","claim_type":"fact","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-7ee8d3af","quote":"share_of_segment_percent: 37.3"},{"evidence_id":"EV-7ee8d3af","quote":"note: missing or wrong unit number dominates - synthetic"}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Direct operational ticket record for the most recent measured quarter."},{"id":"C2","statement":"Apartments are the worst-performing dwelling segment: 84.1% first-attempt success against 90.3% for houses in 2026-Q2.","claim_type":"fact","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-d8895eb0","quote":"value: 84.1"},{"evidence_id":"EV-e64aa734","quote":"value: 90.3"}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Two rows of the same metric series, same period, segmented."},{"id":"C3","statement":"Customers independently report entering the unit number at checkout and it not appearing on the package, which points to an internal data defect rather than customer input error.","claim_type":"fact","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-efad4673","quote":"My apartment number is never included even though I entered it at checkout."},{"evidence_id":"EV-b26a6ee3","quote":"Third time the unit number was missing from the package."},{"evidence_id":"EV-6750be5d","quote":"The address label only shows the street number."}],"support_level":"moderate","rationale":"Multiple independent post-exception comments converge with the ticket-category note, but this is self-reported qualitative data; no system trace has confirmed where the field is dropped."},{"id":"C4","statement":"Bad addresses are a documented cause of failed deliveries at scale: a manual review of 200 failed deliveries found 41% had an incomplete or incorrect address.","claim_type":"fact","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-47eef27a","quote":"A manual review of 200 failed deliveries in one metro area found that 41% had an incomplete or incorrect delivery address."}],"support_level":"moderate","rationale":"Single non-randomised spot-check in one metro area; establishes prevalence of the cause, not the size of any fix."},{"id":"C5","statement":"The size of the improvement from correcting addresses has never been measured, so the expected effect of ALT-04 on first-attempt success is unknown.","claim_type":"fact","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-47eef27a","quote":"No follow-up measurement was taken, so the effect of correction on first-attempt success is unknown."}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Stated explicitly in the experiment record; this is the central gap in the recommendation."},{"id":"C6","statement":"Doing nothing (ALT-01) has an observed, worsening cost: first-attempt success fell from 91.0% in 2025-Q2 to 87.4% in 2026-Q2 while delivery-related support contacts rose from 27.4 to 38.2 per 1,000 deliveries.","claim_type":"fact","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-62f8f8ab","quote":"value: 91.0"},{"evidence_id":"EV-7713e46f","quote":"value: 87.4"},{"evidence_id":"EV-fba2af1f","quote":"value: 27.4"},{"evidence_id":"EV-ef605f46","quote":"value: 38.2"}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Four quarters of the same directly observed metric series; the counterfactual is measured, not inferred."},{"id":"C7","statement":"Cost per delivery is the binding constraint and any per-delivery cost increase needs finance approval before a pilot, which disfavours ALT-08 (agent call-outs) and ALT-10 (mandatory human review of every AI message).","claim_type":"business_constraint","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-92455949","quote":"Cost per delivery is the binding constraint this year. Any proposal that increases per-delivery cost requires finance approval before a pilot may begin."}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Stated policy in the current objectives document."},{"id":"C8","statement":"No driver-facing change can ship before Q3 2026, which blocks ALT-02 outright and undermines ALT-05: access notes captured at checkout have no driver-side consumer this cycle.","claim_type":"technical_constraint","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-15beacab","quote":"The driver application release train is locked until Q3 2026. No change to driver-facing screens can ship before the lock lifts."},{"evidence_id":"EV-986b01eb","quote":"\"Whatever we choose, it cannot touch the driver app before Q3. That is not negotiable.\""}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Engineering constraint document plus corroborating engineering-manager statement."},{"id":"C9","statement":"Exception events reach the warehouse up to 24 hours late, so same-day measurement of any pilot is not currently possible; measurement work is a prerequisite for a credible readout on ALT-04.","claim_type":"technical_constraint","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-15beacab","quote":"Delivery exception events land in the warehouse with a lag of up to 24 hours. Same-day measurement of any intervention is not currently possible."}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Explicit platform constraint; applies regardless of which intervention is chosen."},{"id":"C10","statement":"Address data must stay in its region of origin, and any new vendor processing customer data needs a six-to-eight-week data protection assessment — a gate ALT-06 may trip and ALT-11 is explicitly blocked by.","claim_type":"governance_constraint","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-8dfd4e3c","quote":"Customer address data must remain within its region of origin. We saw the numbers move. We should just turn them on everywhere.\""}],"opposing_citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-47eef27a","quote":"The pilot had no randomised control group. The comparison group was selected after the fact from deliveries in the same period. The difference is not statistically meaningful, and the notification effect cannot be separated from seasonal variation."},{"evidence_id":"EV-47eef27a","quote":"The survey was sent to 15 customers, all of whom had already opted into SMS marketing."}],"support_level":"low","rationale":"The only backing for ALT-07 is that two stakeholders want it; the underlying pilot and survey do not support the claim."},{"id":"C12","statement":"Broad delivery notification enablement is additionally blocked by consent rules and by messaging throughput shared with promotional sends.","claim_type":"governance_constraint","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-8dfd4e3c","quote":"Automated delivery messaging requires recorded opt-in consent. Consent is not transferable between message categories: marketing opt-in does not authorise delivery notifications."},{"evidence_id":"EV-15beacab","quote":"Delivery SMS is routed through the marketing messaging platform and shares a rate limit with promotional sends. At peak promotional volume, delivery messages queue behind marketing traffic."}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Policy plus platform constraint; both independent of the effect-size question."},{"id":"C13","statement":"The AI options have no usable evidence base: the vendor's 30% claim is uncontrolled and undocumented, and automated exception triage has never been tested internally.","claim_type":"fact","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-986b01eb","quote":"The whitepaper does not state its sample size, baseline, comparison method, or the industry the figure came from. No independent evaluation was provided."},{"evidence_id":"EV-47eef27a","quote":"No experiment has tested driver-side workflow changes, and none has tested automated exception triage."}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Absence of evidence is documented in both the stakeholder notes and the experiment record."},{"id":"C14","statement":"ALT-06's FY25 cost blocker is gone, but its integration cost and elapsed time are unknown and it would be a new critical-path dependency at checkout, so it cannot be sequenced ahead of ALT-04 on current information.","claim_type":"technical_constraint","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-15beacab","quote":"Integration effort has not been estimated. The service has never been called from the order path."},{"evidence_id":"EV-15beacab","quote":"Lookups are now bundled at no marginal cost per call, subject to a hard cap of 50 requests per second."}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"Both the removed blocker and the remaining unknowns are stated in the same constraint document."},{"id":"C15","statement":"Repeat-exception customers were never measured, so no option — including ALT-04 — can be justified or targeted on the basis of concentrated harm to high-value customers.","claim_type":"fact","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-8adfb0a2","quote":"synthetic - not measured; field exists but was never populated"}],"support_level":"strong","rationale":"The metric row exists with no value; this is a gap common to every alternative."},{"id":"C16","statement":"Rural exception behaviour is unknown, so the recommendation is not evidenced outside the measured apartment/house split.","claim_type":"fact","citations":[{"evidence_id":"EV-986b01eb","quote":"The Metro West lead asked whether exceptions behave differently in rural areas. Nobody present had the data."}],"support_level":"moderate","rationale":"Recorded as an open question that nobody could answer; limits scope claims."}],"support_level":"moderate","support_basis":"Support is moderate, and only for the apartment segment. It rests on three converging sources for the cause — address_error is 37.3% of apartment exception tickets with unit-number loss named in the ticket notes (EV-7ee8d3af), apartment first-attempt success is 6.2 points below houses (EV-d8895eb0, EV-e64aa734), and multiple post-exception comments describe entering the unit number at checkout and not seeing it on the label (EV-efad4673, EV-b26a6ee3, EV-6750be5d). It is not strong because two things are unmeasured: the effect of correcting an address on first-attempt success (the 2024 spot-check took no follow-up measurement, EV-47eef27a), and the engineering effort, which cannot be estimated until the defect is localised in the order-to-label chain — no estimate exists anywhere in the evidence set, and no cost of an exception has been costed either. Support is comparative as well as absolute: every other option is either blocked (ALT-02, ALT-11), has no measured effect and rests on stakeholder preference (ALT-07), raises per-delivery cost against the binding constraint (ALT-08, ALT-10), lacks a delivery-side consumer this cycle (ALT-05), or is unestimated on the critical path (ALT-06). This claim is evidenced for apartments; it is not evidenced for houses, where address_error is third at 17.0% (EV-beb4932e), nor for rural areas at all.","what_would_change_it":["A localisation spike finding that the secondary address line is NOT being dropped internally — i.e. label fidelity is already high and the loss is at customer input — would move support to low and redirect toward ALT-05 or ALT-06.","A localisation spike finding the loss sits in the driver app or carrier system rather than in our order-to-label path would make ALT-04 unshippable this cycle (EV-15beacab) and promote ALT-03.","An engineering estimate showing the fix exceeds available cycle capacity would move the recommendation to ALT-03 (diagnostic sprint) as the honest use of the quarter.","A randomised follow-up showing address correction produces little or no first-attempt improvement would move support to low for all address-centric options (ALT-04, ALT-06) and raise the relative standing of access-focused work (ALT-09).","Populating repeat_exception_customers (EV-8adfb0a2) and finding harm concentrated in a non-apartment cohort would change the segment scope and could change the recommendation.","A credible estimate for ALT-06 integration showing it is small and can validate address completeness at checkout under the 50 rps cap would make a combined ALT-04 + ALT-06 sequence the stronger plan.","Rural exception data (EV-986b01eb) showing a different dominant cause would refine scope rather than reverse it."],"conditions":["Approve a time-boxed localisation spike (suggest two weeks) before any build commitment. The measured 2026-Q2 position is 87.4% (EV-7713e46f), so the gap to the 93% goal is 5.6 points, not 2.","Populate repeat_exception_customers as part of the same data work, since it is flagged as recommendation-changing and is cheap to add to an analytics workstream."],"tradeoffs":[{"id":"T1","description":"Choosing ALT-04 attacks the largest apartment cause but leaves access_issue — the largest category across all deliveries at 31.1% — untouched this cycle.","gains":["Targets 37.3% of apartment exception tickets, the worst-performing segment","No vendor, no consent gate, no driver-app dependency, no per-delivery cost"],"gives_up":["Access-issue exceptions (31.1% overall) remain unaddressed","Property-manager access work (ALT-09) is deferred with no evidence gathered on building-level concentration"],"alternative_ids":["ALT-04","ALT-09","ALT-05"]},{"id":"T2","description":"Recommending a build over ALT-03 trades measurement rigour for a quarter of momentum, while metrics continue to decline.","gains":["A shippable change in-cycle against a metric that has fallen every quarter","Avoids spending the cycle producing no customer-facing improvement"],"gives_up":["The randomised address-correction study stays undone, so the effect size remains unknown even after the fix","Rural and repeat-exception gaps stay open unless explicitly funded as conditions"],"alternative_ids":["ALT-03","ALT-04","ALT-01"]},{"id":"T3","description":"Declining ALT-07 and ALT-10/ALT-11 means declining what two stakeholders and a VP are asking for.","gains":["Avoids spending the cycle on an intervention whose only prior test showed no statistically meaningful effect","Avoids compounding consent, review-capacity and vendor-assessment gates"],"gives_up":["Stakeholder goodwill; the VP's stated wish for an AI assistant this quarter goes unmet","Any option value from early AI experience, which would need a separate, properly scoped trial later"],"alternative_ids":["ALT-07","ALT-10","ALT-11"]},{"id":"T4","description":"Choosing an internal data fix over vendor address validation forgoes coverage of address errors that originate with the customer rather than in our pipeline.","gains":["No new critical-path dependency at checkout and no 50 rps cap failure mode","No possible six-to-eight-week vendor assessment delay"],"gives_up":["Typos, wrong street numbers and malformed addresses the customer actually entered wrongly go uncorrected","Delays learning whether validation is cheap now that marginal lookup cost is zero"],"alternative_ids":["ALT-04","ALT-06"]}],"experiment":{"id":"EXP-ALT04-UNIT-FIELD","hypothesis":"Secondary address lines entered at checkout are being lost before label generation for a material share of apartment orders; repairing that loss raises apartment first-attempt success and reduces address_error tickets, with no increase in cost per delivery and no reduction in checkout conversion.","method":"Stage 1 (audit, no customer impact): for a sample of at least 2,000 recent apartment orders where a secondary address line was present at checkout, join the checkout record to the generated label payload and measure the label fidelity rate — the share where unit/apartment/suite survived to the label. This quantifies the defect and localises it to a specific hop in the order-to-label chain. If fidelity is already above roughly 95%, stop: the defect hypothesis is disconfirmed and the recommendation fails here, at low cost. Restrict the primary analysis to apartment-segment deliveries. Instrument the pilot cohort so exception events are available faster than the standard 24-hour warehouse lag; if that cannot be arranged, extend the read window and say so in the readout rather than reading a partial quarter.","duration":"2 weeks for the audit and localisation spike; then 8 weeks of staggered rollout and measurement, given the 24-hour event lag and quarterly ticket reporting cadence.","metrics":[{"name":"Secondary-address-line label fidelity rate (apartment orders)","role":"success","definition":"Share of apartment orders with a secondary address line captured at checkout where that line is present and complete on the generated delivery label.","target":"Rise to at least 98% post-fix, from whatever the Stage 1 audit baseline proves to be.","rationale":"This is the direct mechanism the option claims to repair, and the only metric that can be read quickly and unambiguously.
